Extract coefficients, covariance, likelihood and observation counts

Source: R/api-fit-extractors.R, R/api-fit-responses.R, R/api-plotting.R, and 2 more
mfrm_fit_extractors.Rd

Standard R accessors for native many-facet fits. They retain the estimator's coordinates and limitations; extracting a number does not qualify inference.

Describe the retained ratings at the fitted calibration and saved Person estimates, without fitting, scoring Persons again or computing covariance.

Returns all facet-level estimates (person and others) in a single tidy data.frame. Person rows retain their original identifiers; review or transform them before writing the result outside a controlled analysis environment.

These methods inspect the separate result returned by fit_mfrm() with method = "JML", jml_penalty = "jeffreys". The result does not inherit ordinary JML uncertainty or FACETS diagnostics.

Arguments

object

A mfrm_jeffreys_fit result.

type

For fitted() and predict(), "response" returns expected ratings and "prob" category probabilities. For residuals(), "response" returns observed minus expected ratings and "pearson" divides that difference by the conditional rating SD.

...

Unused; additional arguments are rejected.

k

Penalty per free parameter for single-fit AIC(); default 2.

newdata

Must be NULL. These methods describe retained source responses only. For ability scoring from supplied responses use predict_mfrm_units() or score_mfrm_calibration(); those return Person abilities, not predicted rating values. score_mfrm_persons() supplies conditional source-Person scoring for its documented model scope.

x

A mfrm_jeffreys_fit result.

row.names

Ignored (included for S3 generic compatibility).

optional

Ignored (included for S3 generic compatibility).

Value

coef() returns a named numeric vector; vcov() a matrix in the matching default coordinates. MML covariance retains checks, numerical_checks, information_review and cautions attributes when supplied by the interval route. logLik() returns a logLik object; nobs() an integer count; single-fit AIC()/BIC() a numeric value or NA when unsupported. Existing CML covariance coordinates and numeric values are unchanged. No accessor silently computes new Person scores.

A named numeric vector, or for type = "prob" a numeric matrix with one column per modeled category. Attributes include rows, identifiers, score_map, diagnostics (availability, conditional variance and reason), settings (quantity, target, Person basis and limitations) and source_readiness. predict(fit) and fitted(fit) return the same source-rating target.

A data.frame with columns Facet, Level, Estimate, and Extreme. The Extreme column is populated for person rows from the extreme-score flag ("Min" / "Max" / NA); non-person facet rows carry NA in that column by design. Corrected-JML fits additionally retain estimator, correction order, point/covariance status, uncertainty target and structural RootSE columns. Person RootSE is missing; extreme Person flags are "low" / "high" / "none". The estimation_note attribute explains the local-root uncertainty and remaining bias. Ordinary diagnostic attachments do not apply to this estimator; see the Corrected JML section of fit_mfrm_technical_details.

summary() returns Person, facet and step point-estimate tables, checks, category-support evidence and notes. coef() returns the three point-estimate tables. fitted() returns category probabilities in prepared response-row order, with columns from rating_min to rating_max. print() displays the estimator and numerical status. vcov(), confint() and logLik() on this fit stop explicitly: parameter uncertainty and likelihood-based model comparison are not implemented. To estimate common-plan expected-score intervals, use fair_average_table() followed by confint.mfrm_fair_average().

Details

Coordinates. The default coef(fit) is a named numeric vector aligned with both dimensions of vcov(fit). These are free coordinates, not every displayed facet level: anchors and dependent centered coordinates are omitted. MML/JML names such as Rater[1] identify positions within parameter blocks, not literal level names. Steps are free step offsets, slopes are log slopes, and estimated population variance is on the log-variance scale. Population regression coefficients remain on their fitted design scale. CML retains its existing conditional-coordinate names. Use type = "locations" for all saved facet locations with their level labels, and summary(fit) for tables, readiness, constraints and interpretation. Location signs are the fitted model's signs; this accessor does not reorient them as severity. Default confint() intervals use these same coordinates; GPCM positive-slope intervals require explicit parm = "slopes".

type = "persons" returns saved primary Person estimates: MML EAPs and JML point estimates are different targets. Person posterior SDs are not structural standard errors and do not occur in vcov(fit). CML has no Person estimates. Free-coordinate extraction refuses corrected or penalized JML and any fit whose primary estimates are nonfinite: finite optimizer proxies must not replace primary boundary values. Explicit component extraction preserves infinite or missing values in the selected column.

GPCM slope columns. coef(fit, type = "slopes") returns the saved fit$slopes$Estimate, which retains working values for compatibility; it does not select PrimaryEstimate or attach status columns. Read fit$slopes before reporting: PrimaryEstimate is the target's primary value under ParameterStatus and PrimaryEstimateBasis, whereas OptimizerEstimate records the numerical value even when no primary estimate is available. The distinction matters at boundaries and for limiting fits. Neither a finite working value nor an available primary value establishes interval eligibility. See fit_mfrm_technical_details.

Covariance. MML vcov() reuses the same qualified full joint covariance as mfrm_facet_intervals(), including its model/design restrictions and numerical checks. It may reevaluate information and integration, but does not refit. An ineligible source remains an error. For an otherwise eligible ordinary fixed-population RSM/PCM fit, information failure returns an NA matrix with unavailable_reason, checks and cautions; default confint() retains coefficient estimates and reasons in its diagnostics attribute while bounds are missing. No regularized inverse is substituted. If even one dense NA matrix exceeds mfrmr.max_information_bytes, vcov() errors with that reason; use the smaller target-level mfrm_facet_intervals() result. Other MML routes retain their separate qualification checks and error rules. For two-family GPCM, the checked covariance includes free location, step and log-slope coordinates. Use confint(fit, parm = "steps") for separately checked intervals for the expanded step offsets. Dependent centered steps require their constraint transformation; diagonal entries alone do not describe all displayed steps. Nominal coverage across designs has not been established; see mfrmr_gpcm_scope. RSM/PCM singleton-category fits can pass the interval-specific information review while retaining InferenceReady = FALSE; returned cautions and checks explain the small-sample limitation. No count label alone certifies or invalidates this covariance. No JML structural-truth covariance is supplied. CML vcov() reuses saved conditional information. If CML's finite numerical point passed its identification, finite-MLE and stationarity checks but information failed, vcov() returns an NA matrix with unavailable_reason, checks and cautions attributes. coef() and logLik() still expose the retained values; default confint() supplies missing bounds with diagnostic reasons. The warning also limits confidence in point accuracy along weak directions; no regularized covariance or formal inference is substituted. Free-coordinate covariance is not the covariance of a selected component vector or of all displayed levels; use mfrm_facet_intervals() or confint.mfrm_fit() for supported transformations. Comparison-only coef() returns the declared contrast estimates, retaining unavailable rows as NA; its vcov() is available only for native CML conditional comparisons, with the same row/column order.

Likelihood and counts. logLik() returns the retained MML marginal or ordinary JML joint log likelihood, with likelihood_basis and ICReason attributes. Nonunit weights give a weighted objective, not an ordinary sampling likelihood. The df attribute is the free parameter count only when the current information-criterion contract and solution checks permit its use; otherwise it is NA, so AIC() and BIC() are also NA. parameter_count retains the actual dimension separately. JML and two-family GPCM do not gain information-criterion eligibility through these accessors. Corrected JML, penalized objectives and comparison-only fits do not supply a generic logLik() here. For estimated-population/one-family GPCM MML, likelihood qualification may reevaluate solution information.

CML retains its conditional log likelihood and free dimension. Its nobs attribute counts all retained Persons, including extreme totals contributing zero conditional information; informative_persons records nonextreme totals separately. This preserves the existing CML method and is not a new validation of conditional information criteria. Conditional and marginal likelihoods must not be compared. For MML, BIC uses Persons, not rating rows or the sum of rating weights. Counts describe the retained analysis, not omitted input records or an effective sample size under dependence. Use nobs(fit, type = "ratings") to count retained ratings.

For CML, adding extreme-score Persons can increase BIC's penalty even when the conditional likelihood is unchanged. Report both total and informative Person counts. A sensitivity calculation using the latter is -2 * as.numeric(ll) + attr(ll, "df") * log(attr(ll, "informative_persons")), where ll <- logLik(fit) and the informative count is positive. Label this as an alternative penalty convention, not the package's BIC or a validated model-selection rule; neither count resolves dependence or sparse-design asymptotics. Keep the same retained data and conditioning basis in comparisons.

Target. Probabilities are evaluated at saved primary Person estimates: MML uses the saved EAP, while JML uses its primary point estimate. Thus fitted(fit) is a conditional plug-in expectation. Evaluating probabilities at an EAP is different from averaging probabilities over a posterior. For the latter target, use mfrm_response_diagnostics() within its stated model/design scope. These methods do not change diagnose_mfrm() or its legacy diagnostic conventions. Legacy diagnostic helpers use finite JML optimizer proxies and omit variances at or below 1e-10; the primary boundary limits and small positive variances here can therefore give different residuals. Their observation tables retain PersonMeasureBasis, PrimaryPersonMeasure, ConditionalVariance and ResponseReason to explain these differences. Do not assume the routes agree at these limits.

For model-score categories \(k\), let \(p_{ik}\) be the conditional probability. The mean is \(\mu_i=\sum_k k p_{ik}\), the variance is \(V_i=\sum_k (k-\mu_i)^2p_{ik}\), and the Pearson residual is \((y_i-\mu_i)/\sqrt{V_i}\). Rating weights affect estimation but are not multiplied into these per-rating residuals or probabilities. The variance has no artificial positive floor. A zero variance leaves the mean/raw residual available but the Pearson residual missing, with a reason.

A positive/negative infinite JML Person estimate with finite structural calibration has limiting probability one at the maximum/minimum category. These limits use the primary estimate, not the finite optimizer proxy. Other unavailable Person estimates leave the corresponding rows missing. Nonfinite structural estimates, corrected or penalized fits, two-family GPCM, imported fits, CML and comparison-only fits are explicitly refused. CML eliminates Person abilities and does not supply this plug-in target. The supported posterior or corrected-JML routes remain available through mfrm_response_diagnostics().

Rows and scale. Output order is fit$prep$data order, including repeated rating events, and excludes records omitted before fitting. Vector names and probability-matrix row names are retained-row positions. The rows attribute records these positions and original input-row positions where retained metadata permit recovery; unknown positions are NA. No response is silently added or dropped during extraction. The separate identifiers attribute retains Person/facet columns in the same order, including user-supplied facet names that coincide with Row.

Values use the modeled score scale (InternalScore in score_map), as in ordinary plug-in diagnostics. With collapsed categories this differs from the original score labels. The saved score_map attribute retains that mapping; probability columns name the modeled categories. Inspect the map before comparing fitted values with an original, unrecoded data column.

Interpretation. These same-data summaries hold calibration and Person estimates fixed. They omit their estimation uncertainty and are not held-out forecasts, calibrated goodness-of-fit tests or evidence of rater quality. Point calculation does not establish convergence or inference readiness. Read source_readiness and row-specific diagnostics before interpreting values, and keep these attributes when saving the result.

Facet and Level jointly identify a row; Facet = "Person" identifies ability estimates. Use both keys when joining diagnostics: the same level label can occur in different facets. This compact table omits uncertainty and estimate-use restrictions; retain the source fit and read summary(fit).

See fit_mfrm() for the penalty, assumptions and restrictions. checks$ordinary_nll is the ordinary negative log likelihood evaluated at the penalized point; checks$objective also includes the information penalty. Neither is an ordinary maximized likelihood for AIC or testing. category_support describes observed category usage, including missing categories; its ordinary-MLE warnings are not penalty-rank diagnostics.

Interpreting estimates

Estimate is on the fitted latent scale, not the raw rating scale. With default orientation, larger Person values indicate higher ability, larger Rater values greater severity, and larger task/criterion values greater difficulty. Non-Person facets in positive_facets have the opposite score direction. Interpret values relative to the fitted centering/anchors; zero is a scale reference, not absence of ability or severity.

In an additive RSM/PCM with default signs, a Rater difference of 0.5 lowers adjacent-category odds by a factor exp(-0.5) for the same Person and other facet levels. It does not subtract 0.5 raw-score points. GPCM slopes and fitted interactions modify that comparison; use predict.mfrm_fit() for response-scale predictions at specified facet combinations.

Person Estimate is an EAP under MML, conditional on fitted calibration and the specified population model; under ordinary JML it is the fitted Person parameter. EAP shrinkage affects the spread of these estimates, so their empirical SD is not the fitted population SD. Extreme describes observed all-minimum/all-maximum scores, not a statistical outlier test. An extreme score need not give an infinite MML EAP. For uncertainty use diagnose_mfrm() and, for supported structural contrasts, mfrm_facet_intervals(); a missing interval does not erase an available point.

Examples

ratings <- load_mfrmr_data("example_core")
fit <- fit_mfrm(ratings, "Person", c("Rater", "Criterion"), "Score",
  method = "MML", quad_points = 31, maxit = 500)
coef(fit, type = "locations") # Labelled facet locations, including constraints
#>              "Rater":"R01"              "Rater":"R02" 
#>                -0.18381527                -0.30884777 
#>              "Rater":"R03"              "Rater":"R04" 
#>                 0.17950268                 0.31316037 
#>     "Criterion":"Accuracy"      "Criterion":"Content" 
#>                 0.23363879                -0.38997303 
#>     "Criterion":"Language" "Criterion":"Organization" 
#>                 0.09146368                 0.06487055 
coef(fit)                     # Independent coordinates, including steps
#>     Rater[1]     Rater[2]     Rater[3] Criterion[1] Criterion[2] Criterion[3] 
#>  -0.18381527  -0.30884777   0.17950268   0.23363879  -0.38997303   0.09146368 
#>     steps[1]     steps[2] 
#>  -1.21981374  -0.05745669 
nobs(fit)                     # Persons contributing to marginal likelihood
#> [1] 48
nobs(fit, type = "ratings")    # Retained response rows
#> [1] 768
ll <- logLik(fit)
attr(ll, "ICReason")          # Read before interpreting AIC/BIC
#> [1] "Current MML likelihood and solution checks permit information criteria; model comparisons require matched sources."
AIC(fit)
#> [1] 1816.025
# When covariance is qualified, its names match the free coefficients:
# V <- vcov(fit); identical(rownames(V), names(coef(fit)))
ratings <- load_mfrmr_data("example_core")
fit <- fit_mfrm(ratings, "Person", c("Rater", "Criterion"), "Score",
  method = "MML", quad_points = 31, maxit = 500)
expected <- fitted(fit) # Expected ratings at saved EAP abilities
head(data.frame(Observed = fit$prep$data$Score, Expected = as.numeric(expected),
  Residual = as.numeric(residuals(fit))))
#>   Observed Expected   Residual

#> 4 Conditional point calculation; calibration and Person uncertainty are excluded.
#> 5 Conditional point calculation; calibration and Person uncertainty are excluded.
#> 6 Conditional point calculation; calibration and Person uncertainty are excluded.
attr(expected, "settings")         # Read the target and interpretation limits

#> $quantity
#> [1] "expected rating"

# Optional workflow; run the example explicitly as shown below.
# example("as.data.frame.mfrm_fit", run.dontrun = TRUE)
if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
library(mfrmr)

# Saved synthetic MML/RSM analysis of example_operational.
# For your own data, fit a model first; see ?fit_mfrm.
example_fit <- readRDS(system.file("examples", "operational-mml.rds", package = "mfrmr"))
fit <- example_fit$fit

# Extract estimates and select the rows to display
estimates <- as.data.frame(fit)
head(subset(estimates, Facet == "Person")) # First six persons
subset(estimates, Facet == "Rater")       # All raters
subset(estimates, Facet == "Criterion")   # All criteria
} # }
# Long-running workflow; run explicitly when needed.
# example("summary.mfrm_jeffreys_fit", run.dontrun = TRUE)
if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
ratings <- load_mfrmr_data("example_core")
# Each row is one Person's rating by a Rater on a Criterion.
fit <- fit_mfrm(ratings, "Person", c("Rater", "Criterion"), "Score",
  method = "JML", jml_penalty = "jeffreys", rating_min = 1, rating_max = 4,
  category_policy = "preserve")
summary(fit)$persons # Finite penalized Person points, without SEs
summary(fit)$checks$max_gradient # Penalized score-equation diagnostic
plan <- unique(ratings[c("Rater", "Criterion")])
scores <- fair_average_table(fit, reference_plan = plan)
scores$reference_scores # Expected averages under the same plan for all Persons
intervals <- confint(scores, parm = c("P001", "P002"), method = "delta")
intervals[, c("Target", "Estimate", "SE", "Available", "CIEligible")]
# Numerical availability is not a qualification of small-sample coverage.
} # }
